current_law_statement: Primary source: owner-supplied official text of Va. Code § 2.2-3704 complete (subsections A-J), extracted from law.lis.virginia.gov and fetched 2026-08-20 (source_docs/VA_2.2-3704_2026-08-20.txt); history line ends 2023 c. 534, so no 2024-2026 session law has amended the fee/payment subsections (F, G, H, I). Va. Code § 2.2-3704.1 (rights-and-responsibilities posting duty, including the written fee-policy posting) opened on the official code site 2026-08-20; its history ends 2023 c. 599 — also no 2024-2026 amendment. TRAP honored: SB 56 (2026) passed the Senate but was NOT enacted; none of its content (e.g., free labor hours) is imported. Virginia FOIA has NO statutory delegation of fee figures to any regulation or uniform schedule — every operative fee bound lives in § 2.2-3704 itself, so there were no delegated instruments to open. All fee provisions bind 'public bodies' generally, which includes municipalities; the single locality-specific fee provision (electronic method of payment, § 2.2-3704(F) last sentences) is out of the profile per owner decision on payment.method.

resolutions.source_language: a public body may make reasonable charges not to exceed its actual cost incurred in accessing, duplicating, supplying, or searching for the requested records and shall make all reasonable efforts to supply the requested records at the lowest possible cost. ... Any duplicating fee charged by a public body shall not exceed the actual cost of duplication.
resolutions.notes: No statewide per-page number for municipalities. Ceiling is the body's actual cost of duplication, with a companion duty to supply at the lowest possible cost and a prohibition on surplus/overhead fees (VA-0023). City sets its B&W rate under the actual-cost ceiling.

resolutions.source_language: Any duplicating fee charged by a public body shall not exceed the actual cost of duplication.
resolutions.notes: No color-specific rate anywhere in the chapter; the same actual-cost-of-duplication ceiling governs. City may set a distinct color rate provided it does not exceed actual cost.

resolutions.source_language: Any duplicating fee charged by a public body shall not exceed the actual cost of duplication.
resolutions.notes: No oversized/nonstandard-specific rate in the chapter; actual-cost-of-duplication ceiling governs any oversized rate the city sets.

resolutions.source_language: However, such charges shall not exceed the actual cost to the public body in supplying such records, except that the public body may charge, on a pro rata per acre basis, for the cost of creating topographical maps developed by the public body, for such maps or portions thereof, which encompass a contiguous area greater than 50 acres.
resolutions.notes: Specialty reproduction falls under the general actual-cost ceiling. One statutory carve-out: GIS-produced records to non-owners are actual-cost capped, EXCEPT body-developed topographical maps covering >50 contiguous acres may be charged pro rata per acre (VA-0034) — the only above-actual-cost specialty pricing the statute permits.

Coverage: full text of § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) read (owner-supplied official text); § 2.2-3704.1 opened; no VA administrative rule sets FOIA copy fees (no delegation exists). No graduated page-band provision anywhere. A city may adopt volume tiers only insofar as each tier stays within actual cost (VA-0021/VA-0024).

Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. No free-page allowance exists. The prior's snippet (VA-0023 surplus-fee prohibition) is a prohibition on overhead recoupment, not a free allowance; the FERPA scholastic no-charge carve-out (VA-0033) is a record-class exception, not a page allowance. Inspection is free by structure (charges attach to accessing/duplicating/supplying/searching actually incurred).

resolutions.source_language: a public body may make reasonable charges not to exceed its actual cost incurred in accessing, duplicating, supplying, or searching for the requested records and shall make all reasonable efforts to supply the requested records at the lowest possible cost.
resolutions.notes: Search labor is expressly chargeable ('searching for') up to actual cost incurred; no statewide hourly figure. § 2.2-3704.1 additionally requires the body to post a written policy explaining how it assesses access/search charges and the current fee charged (VA-9007) — the city's posted rate is the operative number.

resolutions.source_language: a public body may make reasonable charges not to exceed its actual cost incurred in accessing, duplicating, supplying, or searching for the requested records and shall make all reasonable efforts to supply the requested records at the lowest possible cost.
resolutions.manual_verification: The statute enumerates four chargeable activities (accessing, duplicating, supplying, searching) and never names review/redaction time. Whether exemption-review and redaction labor is chargeable as part of 'accessing'/'supplying' is a scope judgment; VA FOIA Council advisory opinions on this point were not opened in this pass.
resolutions.notes: No separate review/redaction rate or express authorization. If chargeable at all, it is bounded by actual cost incurred and by the surplus-fee prohibition (VA-0023). Flagged for manual verification against FOIA Council opinions.

resolutions.source_language: Public records maintained by a public body in an electronic data processing system, computer database, or any other structured collection of data shall be made available to a requester at a reasonable cost, not to exceed the actual cost in accordance with subsection F.
resolutions.notes: Database/electronic extraction is priced at reasonable cost not to exceed actual cost (subsection G, new row VA-9001). Excision of exempt fields or format conversion is deemed NOT creation of a new record, so it stays inside this cost regime; production in a format not regularly used is not required, but reasonable efforts under agreed terms 'including the payment of reasonable costs' are.

resolutions.unit: enum(never|always|threshold) — no page/hour threshold, no paper-only scope
resolutions.source_language: a public body may make reasonable charges not to exceed its actual cost incurred in accessing, duplicating, supplying, or searching for the requested records and shall make all reasonable efforts to supply the requested records at the lowest possible cost.
resolutions.notes: Labor (accessing/searching/supplying time) is chargeable from the first minute — no free-hours trigger, no page threshold, no paper-only limitation — always subject to the actual-cost ceiling, the lowest-possible-cost duty, and the surplus-fee prohibition. TRAP honored: SB 56 (2026), which would have changed this, was NOT enacted.

resolutions.source_language: No public body shall impose any extraneous, intermediary, or surplus fees or expenses to recoup the general costs associated with creating or maintaining records or transacting the general business of the public body.
resolutions.manual_verification: Whether the actual fringe-benefit cost of the specific responding employee may be counted inside 'actual cost incurred' (as opposed to a percentage overhead surcharge, which is clearly barred) is not expressly resolved by the statute.
resolutions.notes: An overhead/fringe percentage surcharge cannot exist under Virginia law: charges are capped at actual cost incurred, and surplus fees recouping general costs are expressly prohibited. The configurable % is therefore moot for VA cities.

Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened; no administrative fee rule exists. No time-increment or rounding provision. Any increment the city uses must not push charges above actual cost incurred.

Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. No free-labor-hours allowance in current law. TRAP: SB 56 (2026) — which proposed free labor hours — passed the Senate but was NOT enacted; its content is deliberately excluded. History line of § 2.2-3704 ends 2023 c. 534.
Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. No TX § 552.275-style per-requestor periodic free-time ledger exists in Virginia FOIA.

resolutions.source_language: Prior to conducting a search for records, the public body shall notify the requester in writing that the public body may make reasonable charges not to exceed its actual cost incurred in accessing, duplicating, supplying, or searching for requested records and inquire of the requester whether he would like to request a cost estimate in advance of the supplying of the requested records. The public body shall provide the requester with a cost estimate if requested.
resolutions.notes: No dollar/hour threshold: the pre-search written charge notice + estimate inquiry is required on EVERY request (threshold effectively zero), and an itemized estimate is due only when the requester asks. Estimating costs are credited toward overall charges (VA-0029). § 2.2-3704.1 separately requires posting a written fee policy (VA-9007).

resolutions.unit: days from sending of the cost estimate (requester non-response deems the request withdrawn)
resolutions.source_language: If the public body receives no response from the requester within 30 days of sending the cost estimate, the request shall be deemed to be withdrawn.
resolutions.notes: Statute-fixed 30 days (added by 2021 Sp. Sess. I c. 483 era amendments; current through 2023 c. 534). Companion clock rule: the body's response period is tolled between cost-estimate notice and the requester's response (VA-9003). The statute does not specify business vs. calendar days for this 30-day window; plain 'days' read as calendar days.
Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. No revised-estimate-on-variance requirement. Final charges are independently bounded by actual cost regardless of the estimate.

Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. No estimate-validity period. The 30-day non-response withdrawal (VA-9002) binds the requester's reply window, not how long the estimate's figures remain honored.

resolutions.unit: USD (advance determination that charges are likely to exceed $200)
resolutions.source_language: In any case where a public body determines in advance that charges for producing the requested records are likely to exceed $200, the public body may, before continuing to process the request, require the requester to pay a deposit not to exceed the amount of the advance determination.
resolutions.notes: State-fixed $200 trigger; deposit is permissive ('may'). Deposit is credited toward the final cost (VA-9006) and the response clock tolls while the requester's response to the advance determination is pending (VA-9005).

resolutions.unit: % of the advance cost determination (statute states the cap as 'not to exceed the amount of the advance determination', not as a percentage)
resolutions.source_language: the public body may, before continuing to process the request, require the requester to pay a deposit not to exceed the amount of the advance determination. The deposit shall be credited toward the final cost of supplying the requested records.
resolutions.notes: The deposit ceiling equals the full advance determination (i.e., up to 100% of the estimated charges); the city may require any deposit at or under that amount. Mandatory crediting toward the final cost (VA-9006).

resolutions.source_language: the public body may, before continuing to process the request, require the requester to pay a deposit not to exceed the amount of the advance determination. ... Before processing a request for records, a public body may require the requester to pay any amounts owed to the public body for previous requests for records that remain unpaid 30 days or more after billing.
resolutions.notes: Two express PROCESSING gates: (1) the >$200 deposit before continuing to process (VA-0031), and (2) prior unpaid balances 30+ days after billing before processing (VA-9004). No express statutory authorization for a general pay-in-full-before-release gate on the current request's final bill; the statute is silent on conditioning final delivery on payment.

resolutions.source_language: If the public body receives no response from the requester within 30 days of sending the cost estimate, the request shall be deemed to be withdrawn. ... Before processing a request for records, a public body may require the requester to pay any amounts owed to the public body for previous requests for records that remain unpaid 30 days or more after billing.
resolutions.notes: Virginia's nonpayment consequences: (a) deemed withdrawal after 30 days of non-response to a cost estimate (VA-9002 — tied to estimate non-response, not to a billed invoice); (b) prior-debt prepayment gate on future requests once a bill is 30+ days unpaid (VA-9004). No statutory withdrawal clock for nonpayment of a final bill on the current request.

resolutions.source_language: The period within which the public body shall respond under this section shall be tolled for the amount of time that elapses between notice of the advance determination and the response of the requester.
resolutions.notes: Clock effect: TOLLS from notice of the advance (deposit) determination until the requester responds. No grace period and no lapse action are stated for an unpaid deposit — the tolling clause turns on the requester's RESPONSE, and the statute never says what happens if the requester responds but does not pay; flagged in gaps.

Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. No overrun/re-issue rule (no revised-estimate duty, no collection block, no window restart on variance). Actual-cost ceiling independently caps the final bill.
out of scope per owner decision 2026-08-20 — finance-department policy, excluded from state rules profile

resolutions.source_language: a public body may make reasonable charges not to exceed its actual cost incurred in accessing, duplicating, supplying, or searching for the requested records and shall make all reasonable efforts to supply the requested records at the lowest possible cost.
resolutions.notes: The request-level ceiling is the body's actual cost incurred, reinforced by the lowest-possible-cost duty and the surplus-fee prohibition. No statutory dollar maximum.

Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. No de-minimis no-charge floor. Charging is permissive throughout, so a city MAY waive small charges; the only mandatory no-charge category is FERPA scholastic records to parent/guardian/eligible student (VA-0033).

Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. No minimum-fee provision. A flat minimum fee exceeding actual cost on a small request would collide with the actual-cost ceiling (VA-0021) and the surplus-fee prohibition (VA-0023).

resolutions.source_language: Public records maintained by a public body in an electronic data processing system, computer database, or any other structured collection of data shall be made available to a requester at a reasonable cost, not to exceed the actual cost in accordance with subsection F.
resolutions.notes: Electronic-media charges (CD/DVD/USB) are bounded by actual cost (F duplication/supplying; G for database-held records). Bodies must produce electronic records in any tangible medium identified by the requester that the body uses in the regular course of business, including website posting or e-mail where capable.

resolutions.source_language: a public body may make reasonable charges not to exceed its actual cost incurred in accessing, duplicating, supplying, or searching for the requested records and shall make all reasonable efforts to supply the requested records at the lowest possible cost.
resolutions.manual_verification: Postage/mailing is not expressly named; treating delivery cost as part of the actual cost of 'supplying' is a scope judgment (a natural reading, but not an explicit clause).
resolutions.notes: Delivery costs fall under the actual cost of 'supplying' the records; no separate handling-fee authorization (a handling markup would be a surplus fee under VA-0023). Subsection G obliges e-mail/website delivery for electronic records where the body has the capability.

Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. FOIA itself has no certified-copy fee. Certification fees for specific record classes exist elsewhere in the Code (e.g., circuit court clerk fee schedules, vital records) — those are record-specific regimes outside the FOIA municipal-records profile.

Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. No per-recording, per-minute, or free-minutes provision for audio/video. A/V duplication falls under the general actual-cost-of-duplication ceiling (VA-0024).

Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. Virginia FOIA has no commercial-purpose fee schedule or surcharge — the same actual-cost regime applies regardless of purpose. (Eligibility is limited to Commonwealth citizens and qualifying media, but that is an access rule, not a fee schedule.)

Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. No statutory fee-waiver framework: no waiver grounds, no purpose-statement mechanism, no written-denial or waiver-appeal requirement. Because charging is permissive ('may make reasonable charges'), a body retains discretion not to charge — de facto discretionary waiver, city-policy matter. The one mandatory no-charge category is FERPA scholastic records to parent/guardian/eligible student (VA-0033).

Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. No fee-forfeiture-on-late-response provision. A failure to respond is a deemed DENIAL and a violation (§ 2.2-3704(E)) with enforcement consequences, but the statute never strips the body's ability to charge.

Coverage: § 2.2-3704(A)-(J) full text read; § 2.2-3704.1 opened. No repeat-request carry-forward or fee-aggregation threshold. The only cross-request linkage is the prior-debt prepayment gate (§ 2.2-3704(I), VA-9004), which is a payment gate, not aggregation.

new_rules.legal_concept: Electronic-database records at reasonable cost not exceeding actual cost
new_rules.atomic_rule: Public records maintained in an electronic data processing system, computer database, or other structured collection of data shall be made available at a reasonable cost, not to exceed the actual cost in accordance with subsection F.
new_rules.trigger: Request for records held in an electronic data processing system, database, or structured data collection
new_rules.clock_spec: ceiling: actual cost per subsection F
new_rules.source_language: Public records maintained by a public body in an electronic data processing system, computer database, or any other structured collection of data shall be made available to a requester at a reasonable cost, not to exceed the actual cost in accordance with subsection F.
new_rules.notes: Same subsection: excision of exempt fields or format conversion is not creation of a new record; production required in any tangible medium the body uses in the regular course of business (incl. website posting / e-mail where capable); format not regularly used is not required, but reasonable efforts under agreed terms 'including the payment of reasonable costs'.

new_rules.legal_concept: Deemed withdrawal after 30 days of non-response to a cost estimate
new_rules.atomic_rule: If the public body receives no response from the requester within 30 days of sending the cost estimate, the request is deemed withdrawn.
new_rules.trigger: Cost estimate sent; no requester response within 30 days
new_rules.clock_spec: 30 days from sending of the cost estimate; non-response = request deemed withdrawn
new_rules.source_language: If the public body receives no response from the requester within 30 days of sending the cost estimate, the request shall be deemed to be withdrawn.
new_rules.notes: Day type (business vs. calendar) unstated; plain 'days' read as calendar days. Turns on non-RESPONSE to the estimate, not nonpayment of a bill.

new_rules.legal_concept: Response period tolled while a cost estimate awaits the requester's response
new_rules.atomic_rule: The period within which the public body shall respond is tolled for the time that elapses between notice of the cost estimate and the response of the requester.
new_rules.trigger: Notice of cost estimate sent to the requester
new_rules.clock_spec: tolls from notice of the cost estimate until the requester's response
new_rules.source_language: The period within which the public body shall respond under this section shall be tolled for the amount of time that elapses between notice of the cost estimate and the response of the requester.
new_rules.notes: Parallel tolling clause exists for the subsection H advance (deposit) determination — VA-9005.

new_rules.legal_concept: Prior unpaid balances (30+ days after billing) payable before processing a new request
new_rules.atomic_rule: Before processing a request, a public body may require the requester to pay amounts owed for previous records requests that remain unpaid 30 days or more after billing.
new_rules.trigger: New request from a requester with amounts unpaid 30+ days after billing on previous requests
new_rules.clock_spec: fixed trigger: prior amounts unpaid 30 days or more after billing
new_rules.source_language: Before processing a request for records, a public body may require the requester to pay any amounts owed to the public body for previous requests for records that remain unpaid 30 days or more after billing.
new_rules.notes: A processing gate on the NEW request keyed to prior-request debt; the statute does not state a clock effect on the new request's response period while the prior debt is unpaid.

new_rules.legal_concept: Response period tolled while the advance (deposit) determination awaits the requester's response
new_rules.atomic_rule: The period within which the public body shall respond is tolled for the time that elapses between notice of the advance determination and the response of the requester.
new_rules.trigger: Notice of the advance (deposit) determination sent to the requester
new_rules.clock_spec: tolls from notice of the advance determination until the requester's response
new_rules.source_language: The period within which the public body shall respond under this section shall be tolled for the amount of time that elapses between notice of the advance determination and the response of the requester.
new_rules.notes: No grace period or lapse action stated for a deposit that is acknowledged but never paid — the tolling turns on the requester's response, not payment. Flagged in gaps.

new_rules.legal_concept: Deposit credited toward the final cost
new_rules.atomic_rule: The deposit shall be credited toward the final cost of supplying the requested records.
new_rules.source_language: The deposit shall be credited toward the final cost of supplying the requested records.
new_rules.notes: Mandatory crediting; together with the not-to-exceed-advance-determination cap this makes the deposit a prepayment of up to 100% of the estimate, never an add-on.

new_rules.legal_concept: Posted written policy on how access/search charges are assessed and the current fee
new_rules.atomic_rule: The public body's posted rights-and-responsibilities statement must include a written policy (i) explaining how the public body assesses charges for accessing or searching for requested records and (ii) noting the current fee charged, if any, for accessing and searching.
new_rules.trigger: Body is subject to the § 2.2-3704.1 posting duty (state public bodies; localities including towns with population over 250; school boards)
new_rules.source_language: A written policy (i) explaining how the public body assesses charges for accessing or searching for requested records and (ii) noting the current fee charged, if any, for accessing and searching for such requested records.
new_rules.notes: Opened on the official code site 2026-08-20. Quoted clause is the posting-list item; the lead-in sentence establishing the posting duty and the locality scope (towns >250 population) was confirmed on the page but the scope description here is summarized — flag for the verify pass to re-confirm the exact lead-in wording.

applicability_notes: Virginia FOIA runs ONE fee regime for all 'public bodies' — state agencies and localities alike; there is no separate state-agency uniform fee schedule and no delegated fee regulation. Every resolution above is applies_to=all_public_bodies (municipalities fully bound).

The single locality-specific fee/payment provision in § 2.2-3704(F) is the electronic-method-of-payment permission for 'any local public body' (existing VA-0030) — excluded from the profile per the owner's 2026-08-20 payment.method decision.
§ 2.2-3704.1's posting duty (VA-9007) covers state public bodies, localities, and school boards, but among towns only those with population greater than 250 — the one municipal-scope nuance found.
The FERPA scholastic no-charge carve-out (VA-0033) binds any public body holding scholastic records (practically school boards/divisions), not general municipal records.
material_negatives: No statewide per-page copy rate (B&W, color, oversized) — only the actual-cost-of-duplication ceiling.

No free-page allowance, no free labor hours, no per-requestor periodic free time. SB 56 (2026), which proposed free labor hours, passed the Senate but was NOT enacted; § 2.2-3704's history line ends 2023 c. 534.
No labor time-increment/rounding rule; no overhead/fringe surcharge (a % surcharge is affirmatively barred by the surplus-fee prohibition).
No dollar threshold for the estimate duty — the pre-search charge notice is universal, and an estimate is due only on request.
No revised-estimate-on-variance duty, no estimate-validity period, no overrun re-issue rule.
No general pay-before-release gate on the current request's final bill; the only payment gates are the >$200 deposit and prior 30-day-old debts.

No de-minimis floor, no minimum fee, no certification fee (in FOIA), no A/V per-recording/per-minute schedule, no commercial-purpose schedule, no fee-waiver framework, no fee forfeiture on late response, no repeat-request aggregation.
No administrative regulation sets FOIA fees — Virginia FOIA contains no delegation of fee figures to any instrument.
gaps_manual_verification: labor.review.rate: whether exemption-review/redaction time is chargeable within 'accessing, duplicating, supplying, or searching' — check Virginia FOIA Council advisory opinions (not opened this pass).

labor.overheadPct: whether the responding employee's actual fringe-benefit cost may be counted inside 'actual cost incurred' (a % overhead surcharge is clearly barred; per-employee actual fringe is not expressly addressed).
delivery: postage as part of the actual cost of 'supplying' is a natural reading but not an explicit clause.

payment.depositClock: statute gives no grace period or lapse action for a deposit that is acknowledged but unpaid — city policy will have to fill this; the tolling clause turns on the requester's response, not payment.

VA-9007: § 2.2-3704.1 was opened via web fetch; the posting-item clause is quoted verbatim, but the verify pass should re-confirm the lead-in sentence and the towns->250-population scope wording on the official page.
estimate.requesterResponseDays / VA-9002: '30 days' day-type (business vs. calendar) unstated in the statute; read as calendar days.
